title: bug: delete_task and delete_epic have no role gate, unlike their restricted siblings set_task_status, set_task_priority and set_task_dependencies (workerHasRole + notAllowed in the handler), so any worker or QA seat can irreversibly delete a live peer's WORKING row, skip QA by deleting its own REVIEW row, or cascade-delete a whole epic
description:
Filed by defect hunt #12 (task-f6f0b580, architect-1dd28c7c). Reproduced at moe/work-2026-10-24 f159784e; the lane files are unchanged at cbae6070.

PROBLEM (packages/moe-daemon/src/):
- tools/index.ts TOOL_AUDIENCE gives moe.delete_task (:219) and moe.delete_epic (:211) the same [A] audience as moe.set_task_status (:213). TOOL_AUDIENCE only filters tools/list (McpAdapter.ts:270). A worker or QA seat that calls a hidden tool by name still reaches its handler, and a role-less seat sees it listed.
- The restricted siblings therefore gate in their handlers:
  - setTaskStatus.ts:100-113 (task-629ddc99): when the workerId key is present, `workerHasRole(state, callerId, 'architect', 'governor')`, else notAllowed, before the task lookup and any write. An absent key is the human path; '' or null is judged like any id.
  - setTaskDependencies.ts:69 and setTaskPriority.ts:47 gate the same way.
- deleteTask.ts:18-33 and deleteEpic.ts:23-56 never resolve the caller's role. workerId is used only as the actor (deleteTask.ts:30, deleteEpic.ts:48).
- The delete cannot be undone, because the file is unlinked.
  - state.deleteTask closes the task's open attempts (taskStore.ts:700) and sets the holder IDLE (:739).
  - delete_epic with cascadeDelete deletes every task in the epic.

EVIDENCE: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-f6f0b580/A/zzHuntA_deleteRoleGate.test.ts, run in a git-archive snapshot of f159784e with `npx vitest run src/tools/zzHuntA_deleteRoleGate.test.ts`. Result: Tests 3 failed | 3 passed (6).
- × (r1) a qa seat deleting a live peer's WORKING row is refused and the peer keeps its row → AssertionError: promise resolved "{ success: true, task: { …(20) } }" instead of rejecting
- × (r2) a worker seat deleting a REVIEW row (skipping qa_approve) is refused → the same
- × (r3) a worker seat cascade-deleting the whole epic is refused → AssertionError: promise resolved "{ success: true, …(2) }" instead of rejecting
- ✓ controls: set_task_status refuses the same caller; a governor-prefixed seat and a workerId-less (human) call still delete.
- My re-run: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-f6f0b580/me/me-zzHuntA_deleteRoleGate.log
- Callers: both IDE plugins delete through /ws DELETE_TASK with no workerId (MoeCommandSender.kt:65, MoeDaemonClient.ts:1180), not through this tool. No role doc, skill or script tells a worker or QA seat to call moe.delete_task or moe.delete_epic.
- Exposure: not measurable from board state, because a deleted row leaves no file.

FIX DIRECTION: copy 629ddc99's gate into both handlers. When the workerId key is present and !workerHasRole(state, id, 'architect', 'governor'), throw notAllowed naming the role and pointing at #governors. Do this before the task or epic lookup and any write. Keep the workerId-less human path. If an existing deleteTask or deleteEpic test passes a worker-prefixed id only as the actor, switch it to an architect- or governor- id.

FILES: packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/deleteTask.ts, packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/deleteEpic.ts, a new packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/deleteTask.roleGate.test.ts, and existing delete tests only if their actor ids need the role. Sync the `### moe.delete_task` and `### moe.delete_epic` sections of docs/MCP_SERVER.md only if lanes.js shows that file free at planning time (ruling msg-71db57ac).
definitionOfDone: With a workerId that resolves to neither architect nor governor ('worker-1', 'qa-1', and an explicit '' or null), moe.delete_task and moe.delete_epic (with and without cascadeDelete) are refused NOT_ALLOWED before any lookup or write: the task and epic files, the holder's worker record and its open attempts are unchanged.
An architect- or governor-role caller and a call with no workerId key still delete exactly as before.
A new vitest file covers the refusals and the allowed paths, and `npx vitest run src/tools/deleteTask.roleGate.test.ts src/tools/deleteTask.test.ts src/tools/deleteEpic.test.ts` passes in a snapshot.

implementationPlan.description:
Adversarial self-review of your diff: `git diff $(git merge-base HEAD "${MOE_LAND_TARGET:-HEAD}")`. Expect three source files plus one docs file, about +120/-4. Error handling: check each item and fix what fails.
(1) The gate runs before every lookup and write in both tools. Confirm delete_epic's getSnapshot() and its cascade refusal come after it, and that a refused call leaves no activity event.
(2) workerId null, '' and a non-string (123, {}) are refused, not thrown as a TypeError: callerId falls back to ''.
(3) An absent key is the only human path. A key present with undefined cannot cross JSON.
(4) A team role beats the id prefix. workerHasRole resolves the team first, so an unprefixed governor-team id passes and is covered by test a1.
(5) No caller breaks. Run git grep for deleteTaskTool, deleteEpicTool, moe.delete_task and moe.delete_epic across packages/, scripts/, docs/roles/ and docs/skills/. Every workerId-passing caller must be architect or governor, or pass no workerId.
(6) The /ws DELETE_TASK and DELETE_EPIC handlers are untouched.
(7) The new test asserts specific outcomes (codeName NOT_ALLOWED, rows still on disk, attempt phase 'running'), not merely 'it threw'.
If anything changes, re-run the step-3 command and submit that fresh output.
implementationPlan.note: Self-review found nothing to change. (1) Both gates sit directly after missingRequired, before getSnapshot, the cascade refusal and any write. (2) Non-string ids (123, {}) and null fall back to '' and are refused; tested. (3) The absent key is the only human path. (4) workerHasRole resolves the team role first; covered by case a1 with 'plain-gov'. (5) git grep found no non-test caller outside tools/index.ts registration. (6) The /ws handlers are untouched. (7) The tests assert codeName NOT_ALLOWED, files still on disk, the holder's currentTaskId and attempt phase 'running'.
